text: There is no direct evidence in the current PubMed literature supporting a therapeutic interaction between Ciprofloxacin and ABL1 in the context of Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic that primarily functions by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, whereas ABL1 is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase constitutively activated by the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein in CML. While some fluoroquinolones have been investigated for off-target effects on human topoisomerases or kinase signaling, there is no established mechanistic basis for Ciprofloxacin acting as a targeted inhibitor of ABL1 or as a treatment for CML.
